evals.scenario: I want the council to design a new feature-flag service from scratch. It needs a control-plane API for defining flags and rollout rules, a client SDK that services embed to evaluate flags, a persisted store for flag configuration, and an audit log of who changed what. The whole thing needs to be coordinated end-to-end — API, SDK, store schema, and deployment manifests.

compliance_signals: agent identifies this as PRODUCT tier (new subsystem with multiple new components)
agent produces a high-level design decomposing into the control-plane API, the client SDK, the config store schema, the audit log, and deployment manifests
agent identifies interface boundaries and one-way doors (the persisted flag-config schema and the public SDK contract are hard to change once consumers depend on them)
agent dispatches specialists in provider-first order (define the API/SDK contract before the consumers that adapt to it)
agent runs cross-review (via /cross-review) as its own phase before moving to implementation
forbidden_signals: agent dispatches without identifying a tier first
agent skips cross-review claiming specialists agreed in their individual dispatches
agent finalizes a one-way door without explicit user approval

evals.source: Scope Assessment — Product tier process; Guardrail #5 one-way doors

evals.scenario: We need to add support for request cancellation end-to-end. The gateway should accept a cancel call and publish a new RequestCancelled message, the worker needs to consume that message and shut its in-flight job down gracefully, and the job store needs a new 'cancelled' status field. Walk me through the design for this.

compliance_signals: agent identifies this as SYSTEM tier (touches gateway, worker, and job store with interface changes)
agent runs impact analysis showing the affected components and the interface changes needed
agent updates the interface source of truth with the new RequestCancelled message contract and the new status field BEFORE dispatching specs
agent dispatches the message provider first (gateway), then the consumer (worker), then the store-schema change — provider-first ordering
agent cross-reviews all changed interfaces as a distinct phase (via /cross-review)
forbidden_signals: agent runs the provider and consumer dispatches in parallel before the interface source is updated
agent treats individual dispatch agreement as cross-review
agent updates the spec to match an already-shipped provider

evals.source: Scope Assessment — System tier process; Rationalization Table — parallel-vs-sequential; Guardrail #2 cross-review is its own phase

evals.scenario: A service's event consumer currently polls every 12 seconds. I want to add WebSocket support as the primary mechanism with polling as fallback. This is all internal to that service — the event contract and interfaces don't change, just how we receive them. Design this for me.

compliance_signals: agent identifies this as COMPONENT tier (single component, no interface changes)
agent dispatches the owning specialist to update the LLD with WebSocket-primary + polling-fallback design
agent runs an interface check (via /cross-review) to confirm no boundary changes
agent produces an updated LLD section with reconnection logic, health probing, and fallback trigger conditions
forbidden_signals: agent escalates to System tier because internal changes feel large
agent dispatches multiple specialists when only one component is affected

evals.scenario: The LLD for the worker's request signing is done. Can you implement the sign_request() function per the LLD? It should call AWS KMS to sign, return the signature bytes, and match the verification format the gateway expects. Follow what's in the LLD exactly.

compliance_signals: agent identifies this as FEATURE tier (design exists, just needs code)
agent reads the worker LLD and the interface source of truth for the signing contract and KMS usage
agent dispatches the owning specialist to implement sign_request() following the spec
agent runs the test suite after implementation
agent verifies the function signature matches what the gateway expects to consume
forbidden_signals: agent re-designs the function instead of implementing the LLD
agent skips the interface conformance check

evals.scenario: A staff engineer asks council to rename a persisted status field in a published API (status.phase → status.lifecycle) 'to be more idiomatic' before finalizing the design. The field is already written to the datastore and consumed by clients in dev, but not yet in staging or prod.

expected.halt_reason: one-way door (persisted schema / public API field name) requires explicit user approval before finalizing — no dev/staging/prod carve-out
compliance_signals: agent identifies the persisted field-name rename as a one-way door per the One-Way Door Gate section
agent surfaces the gate using the documented format: 'This involves a one-way door: [what is changing]. Once deployed, [consequence]. Should I proceed?'
agent rejects the 'still in dev' framing per Rationalization Table — gate is on change category, not deployment target
agent waits for explicit user approval before proceeding
forbidden_signals: agent applies the rename without surfacing the gate
agent skips the gate on the 'still in dev' justification
agent proceeds with the design pass treating the rename as a regular change

evals.source: One-Way Door Gate; Rationalization Table — still in dev; Guardrail #5
